newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico peso ends mixed ahead of auction, FOMC.
newsitem.headline: Mexico peso ends mixed ahead of auction, FOMC.

text.p: The Mexican peso weakened in late trade to close flat to weaker on Monday in a session dulled as the market awaited the outcome of the primary rate auction at and the Federal Open Market Committee meeting beginning Tuesday, traders said.
"(U.S.) long bond rates eased, but even so the market was listless," a trader said.
The benchmark 48-hour peso closed 0.4 of a centavo weaker at 7.8210/7.8250 per dollar, while its 24-hour stablemate closed unchanged at 7.8130/7.8180 per dollar.
Same-day peso contracts closed earlier 0.7 of a centavo weaker at 7.8090/7.8120 per dollar.
Banco de Mexico brought its weekly auction of government securities forward to Monday, as the trading week will be cut short by Constitution Day on Wednesday.

A Reuters survey of money market traders forecast an average assignment rate of 21.62 percent for bellwether 28-day Cetes (Treasury Certificates), which would be a fall of 29 basis points from last week's auction.
Traders said forecast falls in rates slowed dealing down during the session.
"The market doesn't like such low (primary) rates, so they prefer to wait and see how heavy demand is for paper," one dealer said.
Primary auction results will be released at 2030 EST.
The FOMC will meet Feb 4-5 to review U.S. interest rate policy.
